author: Håvard Pedersen
html: Another setting, which is present in my favorite blog software, Serendipity, is to hold comments for moderation only if the comment is for a blog posting more than 2 weeks old. It could help, depending on how the spambots crawl your site.

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
Jon Cram
html:
I recall one blog requiring users to preview their comment before submitting, although I don't recall whose blog implemented this.

Instead of there being a direct 'submit' button following the comment form, there is only a 'preview' button. This takes the user to a preview of the comment and only then can the comment be submitted.

Apparently this has proved extremely effective in cutting down spam and I just wish I could recall where I saw this.

author: Jesper Rønn-Jensen
Håvard Pedersen
html: Come to think of it, the method I mentioned might be even better if you used the date of the last article comment as a starting point instead of the date of the article itself. That way, active topics can keep themselves open. :)

author: Jermayn Parker
html:
I personally use spam karma and this has been great for me and it also has a "moderation" section which holds 'unsure' comments. I think during my time of using it, i have only had three or four slip through as actual comments.

What I have found however during my blogging ventures is that spammers usually target specific posts and I have also seen one blogger use pingbacks to spam. You can read about these on my blog via these links:\
http://germworks.net/blog/2007/06/28/do-your-spammers-target-specific-posts/\

author: Michael Clark
html: I tweaked Wordpress' wp-post-comments.php file so that the "post" command on the blog post page is actually the IP address of the user. Real users won't see anything different, and they can simply submit a comment. Anyone that spiders my site and later tries to submit a comment with that comment page will be blocked, since the IP address they are coming from doesn't match the comment form they are trying to use. I wrote about it here: http://www.planetmike.com/journal/2007/04/02/blocking-wordpress-comment-spam/
